title: High-Yield Skeletal Muscle Protein Recovery from TRIzol® after RNA and DNA Extraction
author: Yuan Wen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bii3kcgn
materials: To quantify protein concentrations, follow the manufacturer’s protocol for the Bio-Rad RC/DC Protein Assay (5000121). Important point: The RC component of the protein assay is necessary due to the presence of reducing agents in the SDS-urea buffer. Critical Step: Protein samples in the SDS-urea buffer are diluted 10-fold to reduce the total starting amounts of protein and reducing agents in the assay. Protein standards are made using bovine serum albumin solubilized in the respective buffer and are subjected to the same dilution step as the unknown samples ensure consistency.

steps.title: Mince muscle tissue
steps.instruction: Cut the skeletal muscle into small pieces of approximately 10 mg each.

steps.title: Lyse tissue in TRIzol with BCP
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 ml of TRIzol® reagent per tissue piece (≤15 mg) and mix; then add 100 µl of BCP (instead of chloroform) for better phase separation and vortex briefly.

steps.title: Collect RNA aqueous phase
steps.instruction: After incubation, remove the top aqueous (RNA) layer according to the TRIzol® manufacturer’s recommendation.

steps.title: Precipitate and purify RNA
steps.instruction: Follow the TRIzol® manufacturer’s instructions (or an RNA column kit) for RNA precipitation, washing, and resuspension.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 150 µl of 100 % ethanol to the remaining phase, then centrifuge at 5,000 g for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Wash and resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA pellet and resuspend it according to the TRIzol® manufacturer’s protocol or a genomic DNA column purification kit.

steps.title: Transfer protein‑TRIzol‑EtOH aliquot
steps.instruction: Move approximately 0.45 ml of the protein‑TRIzol‑EtOH solution into a 2 ml tube (required for the ~1.8 ml total volume).

steps.title: Add ethanol and BCP for protein precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 650 µl of 100 % ethanol to the tube and vortex; then add 100 µl of BCP, vortex again.

steps.title: Phase separation with water
steps.instruction: Add 600 µl of water, vortex vigorously, then centrifuge at 12,000 g for 5 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Discard aqueous layer
steps.instruction: Remove and discard the upper aqueous layer; the proteins remain in the interphase.

steps.title: Ethanol wash of protein interphase
steps.instruction: Add 700 µl of 100 % ethanol to the interphase/BCP mixture, vortex vigorously, and centrifuge at 12,000 g for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Dry protein pellet
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant and air‑dry the protein pellet at room temperature for 1–2 minutes (do not over‑dry).

steps.title: Dissolve pellet in SDS‑Urea buffer
steps.instruction: Add freshly prepared SDS‑Urea buffer (minimum 100 µl per 10 mg tissue), vortex, and allow the pellet to dissolve at room temperature.
